kuscheln.et: Iterative form of kuschen (“to lie down”) + -eln, from French se coucher. The form is late in standard usage (around 1900), but widespread and significantly older in dialects.

Küster.et: From Middle High German kuster, custer, from Old High German kustor, kostor, from Proto-West Germanic *kustārī.

s: Nur sieben Prozent der Erdoberfläche sind Küstengewässer.
Only seven percent of the earth's surface are coastal waters.

Kuschel.et:
* From Middle High German kuscheln (“to cuddle, snuggle”), from Old High German koschen.
* From Kusch + -el (diminutive suffix).
* Borrowed from Yiddish קושל (kushl), pet form of יקותיאל (yekusiel).
* Borrowed from Czech Kužel, from kužel (“distaff, cone”).

kusch.et: Originally hunting jargon, from French couche! (“lie down!”), from coucher. The use for “shoo” may or may not be the same word, see ksch for more.

s: to knuckle under, to kowtow (to act submissively)

Frohlocke nicht, wenn ich für diesmal kusche,
Wart nur, wart nur, bis ich dich einmal dusche!
»Bei denen heißt's noch immer, wenn unsereins den Mund auftut: Kusch dich! zu Hause — wie in der Bewegung,« sagte eine andere langjährige Parteigenossin.
